_meta.indication: KEYTRUDA QLEX is a combination of pembrolizumab (PD-1-blocking antibody) and berahyaluronidase alfa, indicated for solid tumor indications approved for IV pembrolizumab, including first-line metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC (with pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy, no EGFR or ALK aberrations) and unresectable or metastatic melanoma

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled, parallel-group, multiregional non-inferiority trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with treatment-naive metastatic NSCLC with no EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 genomic tumor aberrations
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Dual primary PK endpoints: Cycle 1 AUC(0-6 weeks) and Cycle 3 (steady state) Ctrough
pivotal_trials.n: 377 patients randomized (2:1): 251 pembrolizumab SC + chemo, 126 pembrolizumab IV + chemo
pivotal_trials.result: Both PK endpoints met the pre-specified criteria (lower bound of 90% CI of GMR at 0.8 or above): Cycle 1 AUC(0-6wks) GMR 1.14 (96% CI: 1.06, 1.22); Cycle 3 Ctrough GMR 1.67 (94% CI: 1.52, 1.84). [Note: the 96%/94% CI levels are copied verbatim from the review and appear to be OCR artifacts for 90% CI.] Efficacy endpoints were descriptive: ORR 45% (95% CI: 39, 52) (SC) vs 42% (95% CI: 33, 51) (IV); median PFS 8.1 months (95% CI: 6.3, 8.3) vs 7.8 months (95% CI: 6.2, 9.7) (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.78, 1.43); median OS (updated analysis) 19.4 months (95% CI: 17.2, NR) vs 17.7 months (95% CI: 13.9, NR) (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.68, 1.25). There were no notable differences in PFS or OS between the SC and IV arms

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) with SC + chemotherapy were nausea (25%), fatigue (25%), and musculoskeletal pain (21%). Serious ARs in 39%; fatal ARs in 10% (including pneumonia 3.2%). Local injection site reactions was the only newly identified signal vs IV. Immune-mediated adverse reactions may be severe or fatal
target_moa: Pembrolizumab is a humanized IgG4 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds PD-1 and blocks the PD-L1/PD-L2 ligands; berahyaluronidase alfa is an endoglycosidase that temporarily breaks down the subcutaneous extracellular matrix to enhance dispersion and absorption of pembrolizumab
modality: Monoclonal antibody (pembrolizumab, IgG4 kappa mAb) co-formulated with a recombinant human hyaluronidase (enzyme) permeation enhancer, for subcutaneous administration

rems.type: A REMS was determined not required to ensure safe and effective use

companion_dx_detail: No device or companion diagnostic test was reviewed as part of this application

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee, as no significant efficacy or safety issues required external input

description.text: Added new indication in combination with enfotumab vedotin as neoadjuvant then adjuvant treatment for adults with muscle invasive bladder cancer ineligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for a new indication for Keytruda Qlex, in combination with enfotumab vedotin, as neoadjuvant treatment, and then continued after cystectomy as adjuvant treatment for the treatment of adult patients with muscle invasive bladder cancer who are ineligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy.

description.text: Added indication in combination with paclitaxel, with or without bevacizumab, for platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal carcinoma with PD-L1 (CPS≥1) after one or two prior regimens

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for a new indication for Keytruda QLEX (pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph) in combination with paclitaxel, with or without bevacizumab, for the treatment of adult patients with platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal carcinoma whose tumors express PD-L1 (CPS\geq1) as determined by an FDA-authorized test and who have received one or two prior systemic treatment regimens.

description.text: Added a Patient Experience section (14.2) with patient-reported preference results for subcutaneous coformulation over IV pembrolizumab

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for the addition of a Patient Experience section (14.2) of the U.S. Prescribing Information labeling, to incorporate patient-reported preference results from Study MK-3475A-F11, entitled “A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate Patient Reported Preference for Subcutaneous Pembrolizumab Coformulated with Hyaluronidase (MK-3475A) Over Intravenous Pembrolizumab Formulation in Participants with Multiple Tumor Types.”

surrogate_endpoint.text: Tumor response rate and durability of response, for the TMB-H cancer indication, which is approved under accelerated approval (as is IV pembrolizumab); the FDA review teams recommended that pembrolizumab SC also be approved under accelerated approval for this indication

citations.quote: pembrolizumab IV is approved for tumor mutational burden-high cancers under accelerated approval and pembrolizumab SC should also be approved under accelerated approval for this indication.
This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response.

KEYTRUDA QLEX is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with unresectable or metastatic tumor mutational burden-high (TMB-H) [\ge10 mutations/megabase (mut/Mb)] solid tumors, as determined by an FDA-approved test [see *Dosage and Administration* (2.1)], that have progressed following prior treatment and who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Accelerated Approval PMR carried over verbatim from the pembrolizumab IV PMR under BLA 125514: submit final report and datasets from trials evaluating ORR and duration of response to verify clinical benefit in TMB-H solid tumors

citations.quote: Pembrolizumab SC will be subject to the accelerated approval postmarketing requirement (PMR) that was issued for pembrolizumab IV under BLA 125514 for the indication for tumor mutational burden-high (TMB-H) cancers, as this PMR has not been fulfilled and the indication currently remains under accelerated approval.

Submit the final report and datasets from clinical trials evaluating overall response rate and duration of response, to verify and describe the clinical benefit of pembrolizumab in adult and pediatric patients with unresectable or metastatic tumor mutational burden-high (TMB-H)

basis.text: The BLA 761467 was designated Priority review

summary.text: This priority-review BLA for subcutaneous pembrolizumab co-formulated with berahyaluronidase alfa received traditional approval for solid tumor indications previously approved for IV pembrolizumab based on PK bridging (Study MK-3475A-D77), except the TMB-H cancer indication, which was granted under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability with a confirmatory PMR

citations.quote: the FDA review teams recommend traditional approval of pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph for subcutaneous injection for adult and pediatric (12 years and older) solid tumor indications approved for the intravenous formulation of pembrolizumab at the time of the original BLA submission, except for tumor mutational burden-high cancers
pembrolizumab SC should also be approved under accelerated approval for this indication.
